title: The Past Simple
subtitle: Tell any story about yesterday - correctly

beats.caption: Yesterday, I <v>walked</v> to the hills, and I <v>saw</v> three sheep!
I <v>didn't see</v> the moon... but I <v>saw</v> a beautiful sunset.

say: Walked. Saw. Didn't see. Mia is telling us about yesterday, and she is using the past simple.
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to tell any story about the past, clearly and correctly. Let's start.

data.heading: When do we use the past simple?
points: At a finished time in the past
The time is clear (or we know it)

say: We use the past simple for actions that started and finished in the past.
The action is finished, and the time is finished too. Yesterday is finished. Last week is finished.
Often we say the time: yesterday, last summer, in twenty twenty. And sometimes we don't say it, because the listener already knows it from the story.
beats.chapter: When we use the past simple

data.heading: Positive sentences
data.note: Same form for I, you, he, she, it, we, they!

say: Here is the good news. The past simple is the same for every person. I walked, you walked, she walked, they walked. No extra s, no changes.
For most verbs, we just add e d. Walk becomes walked.
Play becomes played.
Watch becomes watched.
Visit becomes visited.
Remember: the same form for I, you, he, she, it, we and they.
Now, spelling. Most verbs simply take e d: walk, walked.
If the verb ends in e, add only d: live, lived.
If the verb ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i e d: study, studied.
But if there is a vowel before the y, just add e d: play, played.
And for short verbs that end consonant, vowel, consonant, double the last letter: stop, stopped. Plan, planned.
The e d ending has three different sounds. Listen.
After sounds like p, k, s, sh and ch, we say t: walked, watched, stopped, kissed.
After voiced sounds and vowels, we say d: played, lived, cleaned, opened.
And only after t or d, we add a new syllable, id: wanted, visited, needed, started.
So we never say walk-ed. We say walked. One syllable.
Let's watch Mia's evening again. Yesterday evening, Mia walked through the grass. She stopped near the sheep, and she counted them: one, two, three.
beats.caption: Mia <v>walked</v> through the grass. She <v>stopped</v> near the sheep.

say: Many common verbs are irregular. They don't take e d. You need to learn them.
Go, went. I went to the hills.
See, saw. She saw three sheep.
Have, had. We had dinner.
Eat, ate. He ate an apple.
Come, came. They came home late.
Take, took. I took a photo.
Make, made. Grandma made soup.
Buy, bought. Dad bought a map.
Here's a tip: learn them in small groups of five, and say each one in a real sentence about your own day.

data.heading: The verb BE: was / were
rows: I was happy. It was cold.

say: Before negatives, one special verb: be. In the past, be has two forms: was and were.
I, he, she and it take was. I was happy. It was cold.
You, we and they take were. We were at home.
The negative is wasn't or weren't. She wasn't tired. We don't use didn't with be.
And questions start with was or were. Were you in the park?

data.heading: Negative sentences
data.note: didn't = did not. After didn't, use the BASE verb: didn't go (not didn't went).

say: To make a negative, we use didn't, and then the base verb.
I didn't see the moon.
She didn't walk to school.
We didn't eat breakfast.
They didn't go home.
Very important: didn't already shows the past. So the main verb goes back to its base form. We say didn't go, never didn't went.

beats.caption: I <v>didn't see</v> the moon... but I <v>saw</v> a beautiful sunset.

data.heading: Questions and short answers
pairs: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

say: For questions, put did before the subject, and again, use the base verb.
Did you see the sunset? Yes, I did. Or: no, I didn't.
Did Mia walk home? Yes, she did.
With question words, did comes after them. Where did she go? She went to the hills.
What did you eat? I ate soup.
These words tell us the time is finished, so they love the past simple.
Yesterday. Last night. Last week. Last summer.
Two days ago. A year ago. Ago always comes after the time.
In twenty twenty. When I was a child.
And this morning, but only when the morning is already finished.

data.heading: Common mistakes (Arabic speakers)
rows: I was go to school yesterday.
I visit my grandma last week.
I visited my grandma last week.

say: Let's fix some very common mistakes.
He didn't went home. No. After didn't, use the base verb: he didn't go home.
Did you saw the sunset? No. Did you see the sunset?
I was go to school yesterday. In Arabic we can think was plus a verb, but in English we just say: I went to school yesterday.
She goed to the park. Go is irregular: she went.
I visit my grandma last week. Last week is finished, so: I visited my grandma last week.
Now, let's practise your speaking. Listen, and repeat after me. Say it out loud!

data.heading: Mia's evening
data.sub: Listen and notice the past simple

say: Now, let's hear the whole story of Mia's evening. Listen, and notice every past simple verb.
Yesterday evening, Mia walked through the soft grass. She saw some sheep near the old wall, and she stopped to count them.
beats.caption: Mia <v>walked</v> through the grass. She <v>saw</v> some sheep and <v>stopped</v> to count them.
Then I <v>walked</v> home, and I <v>had</v> dinner with Grandma.

say: The sun went down. Mia didn't stay in the field. She walked home before dark.
beats.caption: The sun <v>went</v> down. Mia <v>didn't stay</v>. She <v>walked</v> home.

data.heading: Your turn!
data.sub: Pause the video if you need more time

say: Now it's your turn. Choose the correct answer. You have five seconds for each question.

beats.say_answer: Went. Go is irregular: go, went.
Watch. After didn't, we use the base verb.
Did. Did you see Mia last night?
Lived. The verb ends in e, so we add only d.

data.heading: Remember
items: Irregular verbs: learn them in groups
didn't + base verb / Did ... + base verb?

say: Let's remember. The past simple is for finished actions at a finished time.
It's the same for every person. Regular verbs take e d, with a few spelling rules, and the ending has three sounds.
Irregular verbs need to be learned. And in negatives and questions, we use did, with the base verb.

data.heading: Your homework
data.task: Write five sentences about YESTERDAY in the comments.

say: Here is your homework. Write five sentences about what you did yesterday in the comments. I will read them.
If this lesson helped you, subscribe, and I'll see you in the next lesson: the past continuous. Goodbye!
